items.title: Pittsfield draft rules set 10-acre minimums, 500-foot buffers for data centers after public survey
items.dek: Pittsfield Charter Township Planning Commission holds a public hearing tonight on a draft ordinance that would restrict High Resource Demand Facilities like data centers to industrial zones only, with minimum lot sizes of 10 acres for large-scale projects and 500-foot setbacks from homes, schools and parks. A May-June survey drew over 300 responses.
items.source: Pittsfield Charter Township Planning Commission agenda
items.findings: Draft ordinance defines HRDFs by thresholds including >10 MW electric demand, >100 gpm average daily water use and >50,000 gallons/day sanitary discharge | Large-scale data centers require 10-acre minimum lots, 60% max coverage, 45-foot height limit and 500-foot setbacks from residential zones or schools | All HRDFs allowed as conditional use in Industrial zones only and must go through process with mandatory pre-application conference, community engagement plan and neighborhood meetings 21-60 days before hearings | Township collected public input during May and June 2026 through a Public Survey, receiving over 300 responses | Moratorium on new data centers adopted in 2025, set to expire November 2026
items.perspective: The township board adopted a temporary moratorium in 2025 while staff prepared the draft over the past six months to address topics such as energy use, water conservation, noise, traffic, environmental protection, mitigation, and long-term site management.
